tests.description: Four theme-parametrized browser-component regressions using production PhotoGridItem and CSS.

fixture_needs: Browser-local typed PhotoWithUrls factory producing valid 240x240 white PNG data URLs; two ownership variants; deterministic IDs.
Vite HTML/React harness importing production PhotoGridItem and src/index.css, with observable selection callback IDs.
Self-contained browser measurement helper for decoded white image, computed sRGB colors/contrast, ancestor opacity, and geometry.
Reuse tests/support/merged-fixtures.ts with authSessionEnabled:false; no additional merged fixture or auth provider.

additional_files.description: Proposed factory for parent aggregation step 3C.
Proposed Vite harness entrypoint for parent aggregation step 3C.
Proposed real-component rendering harness for parent aggregation step 3C.
Proposed reusable browser probe shared by four cases for parent aggregation step 3C.

summary: Generated 2 P1 contrast and 2 P2 preservation cases, one for each theme. Browser component scope only; no authenticated gallery/API claims or DB writes. Code is proposed in JSON only, no active files or test execution.
validation_notes: Original /90 will fail the same P1 assertions on alpha and composite contrast. Recommended negative control: temporary response transform of production PhotoGridItem module, replacing bg-pink-600 with bg-pink-600/90 for a separate validation run; do not mutate production files.
All selectors are backed by production markup or explicitly defined harness markup. Browser runtime verification is deferred to parent step 4 because the harness is not activated yet.
No HAR recording is needed: this component has no application API traffic; PNGs are generated in the browser and only external static font stylesheet traffic is stubbed.
All additional files are proposals for parent step 3C aggregation, not written into active tests; step 3B generated no fixture registrations.

The white PNG represents the adverse input. The spec asserts opaque background and every label ancestor opacity equals 1, so computed source-over contrast is valid without assuming a transparent ancestor composition.
